<p>There is a quiet truth most people already understand, even if they don’t always say it out loud. When something is simple and fair, people trust it. When it feels confusing or controlled by too many middle layers, people hesitate. Ticketing has lived in that second world for a long time.</p><p>If you have ever tried to buy a ticket and wondered if it was real, or paid more than expected at checkout, then you already understand the problem. It is not just about tickets. It is about trust.</p><p>Onchain ticketing is not trying to reinvent events. It is trying to restore the trust that got lost.</p><hr><h2 id="h-a-better-way-not-a-new-way" class="text-3xl font-header !mt-8 !mb-4 first:!mt-0 first:!mb-0">A Better Way, Not a New Way</h2><p>It’s not about making ticketing more complicated. It’s about removing the parts that made it confusing and insecure in the first place. </p><p>It’s not about forcing people to learn something new either. It’s about making the experience feel more natural, something that just works without needing extra effort or second-guessing.</p><p>And it’s not about replacing event organizers. It’s about giving them back control over their own audience. </p><p>This is where <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow ugc" class="dont-break-out" href="https://app.unlock-protocol.com/event"><strong>Unlock EVENTS</strong></a><strong> </strong>comes in, taking something that used to feel heavy and turning it into something you can set up in minutes, without losing clarity or control.</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/7531dc3aace3a810db6479265811735d119169ae69a888b6df6e216d8cacf1f8.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><hr><h2 id="h-so-what-is-unlock-events-really" class="text-3xl font-header !mt-8 !mb-4 first:!mt-0 first:!mb-0">So What Is Unlock EVENTS, Really?</h2><p>At its core, <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow ugc" class="dont-break-out" href="https://app.unlock-protocol.com/event"><strong>Unlock EVENTS</strong></a> is a simple way to create and sell tickets that live 'onchain' (on a blockchain). No stress, no overthinking. Instead of your ticket being locked inside one app or platform, it goes straight to the buyer’s wallet. That means<strong> it’s easy to check, hard to fake, and actually is something you own</strong>, not something you’re borrowing.</p><p>The best part is you don’t even have to think about all the 'how it works' stuff. From your side, it feels like setting up a normal event page. Add your details, share your link, and you’re good. Clean, simple, and it just makes sense.</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/d74307c6b5d34f22f2e6fd902ad052afeef49be09c999498f82c171a34d6d3e5.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><hr><h2 id="h-step-by-step-how-to-sell-tickets-using-unlock-events" class="text-3xl font-header !mt-8 !mb-4 first:!mt-0 first:!mb-0">Step-by-Step: How to Sell Tickets Using Unlock EVENTS</h2><p>Let’s walk through it slowly, the same way you would explain it to a friend.</p><p><strong>Step 1: Create Your Event<br></strong>You start by setting up your event, and honestly, this part feels like filling out a form. You give your event a name, write a short description, pick a date and time, and that’s it. No weird setup, no confusion. You’re just telling people what you’re planning, the same way you would anywhere else online.</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/c96ab8a7b526a30c52168ce441e3f883e2ffabb90dceed5218b03b0c2ce48159.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><p><strong>Step 2: Set Your Ticket Details<br></strong>Now you decide how your tickets should work. You choose the price or make it free, set how many tickets are available, and decide if people can resell or transfer them. This is where it quietly feels different. It’s not some platform adding random fees or rules behind the scenes. You’re the one in control of how access works.</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/fb2808c5a09249121e2fff03d60da9738f530187fe0095ba48952707c2520932.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><p><strong>Step 3: Publish and Share<br></strong>Once everything looks good, you hit publish. You get a link, and that link is your whole ticket page. From here you can share it anywhere, such as X, WhatsApp, via Email, etc. The special ingredient: If you want to embed it into your own website's event page. No problem at all, it just takes one little extra step of creating a checkout URL with Unlock:</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/9f2f66d72e43ef67f62340316d67c4af43c43d542a9ba34a459d60dcf6e75cbb.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><p>Anyone with the link can open it and mint a ticket (unless you set different conditions, which is also a possibility). There is no waiting room. No hidden steps. No strange redirects.</p><p><strong>Step 4: People Mint Their Tickets<br></strong>When someone clicks your link, they just mint their ticket. It goes straight into their wallet (or email if they don't have a wallet, Unlock creates one for them). Not a screenshot, not a PDF that can be copied and passed around. It’s something they actually own. For them, it feels quick and smooth. For you, it means no stress about fake tickets showing up at your event.</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/49a046e8c2c790387b6e5a844d96b32c729167891cb5f130e959dae6fa40ffdb.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><p><strong>Step 5: Manage Your Attendees<br></strong>As people get tickets, you can see your attendee list in real time. And this part hits differently. It’s not just a list of buyers, it’s your actual community. These are the people showing up. Later, you can invite them again, reward them, or just stay connected. It doesn’t end after a single event and isn't bound to a single platform.</p><figure float="none" data-type="figure" class="img-center"><img src="/images/blog/event-tickets-onchain-with-unlock/ec26004aea8b4bb7b4df2c5bf5a65c5df4f6f3b5815e8422441d0fc150846e68.png" blurdataurl="data:image/png;base64," nextheight="2064" nextwidth="3840" class="image-node embed"><figcaption htmlattributes="[object Object]" class="hide-figcaption"></figcaption></figure><p><strong>Step 6: Check People In<br></strong>On the day of the event, if it is in person, check-in is simple. Every ticket comes with a QR code; you scan it, and you’re done. No app crashing at the gate, no long lines because something isn’t working, no second-guessing if a ticket is real. It just works the way it should: Simple and secure.</p><hr><h2 id="h-what-changes-for-attendees" class="text-3xl font-header !mt-8 !mb-4 first:!mt-0 first:!mb-0">What Changes for Attendees</h2><p>From the attendee’s side, the experience becomes easier and more trustworthy. By using blockchain-secured ticketing with Unlock, they can be reassured that:</p><ul><li><p>The ticket is real</p></li><li><p>The price is what they saw</p></li><li><p>They own it</p></li></ul><p>If you allow transfers, they can safely pass their ticket to someone else. It’s not about turning them into 'crypto users.' It’s about making the process feel reliable again.</p><hr><h2 id="h-what-changes-for-organizers" class="text-3xl font-header !mt-8 !mb-4 first:!mt-0 first:!mb-0">What Changes for Organizers</h2><p>For organizers, this shift hits a bit deeper. You’re no longer handing your audience over to some platform and hoping for the best. You’re building your own connection with them. Payments come straight to you, you decide how tickets work, and you choose how to keep people engaged even after the event. It just feels more direct, like you’re actually in charge of your own space.</p><p>That said, it’s only fair to mention there’s a tiny learning curve at the start. If you’ve never used a wallet before, setting things up might take a few extra minutes. But once you get past that first step, everything else feels lighter. You spend less time dealing with issues and more time focusing on the actual event. </p><p>And on the bright side, Unlock is a community and always ready to help out! We now even offer a service to support you on your journey in a much  more dedicated way. Reach out if you are interested in our <a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow ugc" class="dont-break-out" href="https://t.me/+bNlNMrPjb5BhZjJi"><strong>Telegram channel</strong></a>.</p><hr><h2 id="h-a-balanced-way-to-look-at-it" class="text-3xl font-header !mt-8 !mb-4 first:!mt-0 first:!mb-0">A Balanced Way to Look at It</h2><p>It would be easy to say this fixes everything overnight, but it doesn’t. Some people still prefer what they’re used to, some events might not need this level of control, and some organizers will take their time figuring it all out, which is completely fair. Still, even with all that, this new direction clearly offers more benefits than drawbacks for both the organizers and attendees. </p><p>At the start, we talked about trust.
